# gointervals

> Free browser timers: interval (work, rest, rounds), meditation with interval bells, Tabata, EMOM and Pomodoro. No account, no ads, no server. Timing is timestamp-based so it does not drift when a tab is throttled or a phone sleeps. Keeps the screen on, beeps with generated tones, works offline after the first visit. Built by Nimish Nandwana (https://nimishnandwana.com).

Site: https://gointervals.com
Source: https://github.com/nimi0112/gointervals
License: MIT, open source. Content may be quoted with attribution. Issues and contributions: https://github.com/nimi0112/gointervals/issues

## Timers

- [Home](https://gointervals.com/): the five timers, a short guide and common questions.
- [Interval timer](https://gointervals.com/interval): work 1–3600 s, rest 0–3600 s, rounds 1–99; default 30 min work, 5 min rest, 8 rounds; rest 0 makes a "beep every N minutes" timer.
- [Meditation timer](https://gointervals.com/meditation): one clock for the whole session, optional interval bells (default every 10 minutes of 30), optional start and end bells, no ticks.
- [Tabata timer](https://gointervals.com/tabata): fixed 20 s work, 10 s rest, 8 rounds, 4 minutes.
- [EMOM timer](https://gointervals.com/emom): interval 15–300 s (default 60), total 1–99 minutes (default 10).
- [Pomodoro timer](https://gointervals.com/pomodoro): 25/5/15 with 4 focus sessions, one finite cycle, all editable.

## Other

- [About](https://gointervals.com/about): who built it, source and author links, what is stored in the browser and how to clear it.
- Keyboard: Space start/pause/resume, Esc stop (asks first), R reset (asks first).
- Removed routes /stopwatch, /timer and /timer/* redirect to the closest surviving timer.
